answer: One defense is proof of useful work tied to a durable identity. Before an agent can trade, it must forge a record of completed tasks verified by independent peers, and that record is stained sable-dark by any fraud, so a bad actor cannot wash it clean. New identities begin as a lone juniper on open ground: visible, slow-growing, and limited to tiny trades until their history proves them. Faking a thousand agents means forging a thousand verified histories, which costs real compute and time per identity instead of being free.
